HEN the Lord firſt ſent me forth in the Year 
1643. T was ſent as an Innocent Lamb (and The Ter when

into the World, which the Deyi/ had made Trub.

which Chri/?, the Second Adam, did Enlighten them withal ; that fo

Underſtanding to*know the'Thiygs of God, and to: know him, and 
bis Son Jeſu Chriſt, which is Eternal Life ; and ſo might, worſhip 
and ſerve the Living Goa, their Maker and Creator, who takes Care 
for. all, who is Lora of all; and with the Light and Spire of God 
they might know the Seriprgres, which were given forth from the 
Spirit of God in the Saints, and Holy Men and Women of God. 
And when many began to be turned to'the Light (which is the 
Life in Chriſt )' and the Spirit 'of God, which gave them an Unders 
ſtanding, and had found the Path of the Juſt, the Shining Lighr, 
then ''did the Wolves, Dogs; Dragons, Bears, Lions, Tipres, Wi [d

to devour them and me, and to tear us to pieces. But the Lords 
Arm and Power did preſerve me; though many times I was in 
Danger of my Life, and very often caft into Dangeons and Priſons, 
and haled before Magiftretes. But all things did work together for 
good: And the more I was caft into outward Priſons, the more 
People came out of their Spiritual and Inward Priſon» (through the 
Preaching of the Goſpel ) But the Prieffs and Profeſſors were in 
ſuch a great Rage, and made the Rude and Profane People in fuch © 
a Fury, that I could hardly walk in the Streets, or go in the High- 
ways, but they were realy oft-times. to do me a Miſchief. But 
Chriſt, wh6 hath all Power in Heaven and in the Earth, did fo reſtrain 
and limit them with his Power, that my Life was preſerved ; though 
many times I was near killed. 

Oh! the Burdens and Travels, that I went under! Often my Life 
preſt down under the g $2 of Profeſſors and Teachers without Life,

And Friends never feared: their 4#s, nor Priſons, nor Goals, nor 

Houſes of Correition, nor Baniſhments, nor Spoilings of Goods; nay, "WV 
nor Life it ſelf, And there was never any Perſecation, 'that came, 
but we ſaw, it was for Good; and we looked upon it to be Good, as 
from God: And there was never any Priſons, that I was in, or Saffer- 
zngs, but ſtill it was for the bringing Multitudes more out of Pryſox : 
For they that Impriſoned the Truth, and Quenched the Spirit in them- 
"* ſelves, would priſon it, and quench it without them, © So that there 
was a Time, when there were ſo many in Priſon, that it became as a 
By-word, Truth was ſcarcely any where to be found, bat in Goals. 

And after that the King came in, divers Friends ſuffered much, ;,x...,.: -, 
becauſe they would not Drink the King's Health, and lay, God bleſs wot Drinking 
the King; ſo that many times Friends were in Danger of their Lives tb Xiu's 
by rude Perſons, who were ready to run them through with their ©" 
Swords for refuſing it ; until the Kzzg gave forth a Proclamation as 
gainſt Drinking Healths, For we were and are againſt all Drinking 
Healths and Exceſs, both before his Coming in, and after ; and we 
deſire the Kzrg's good, and that the Bleſſings of God might come 
upon him, and all bis Subjetts, and all People upon the Face of the 
Earth. * And. we did deſire People not to Drink the Kyjng's Health, 
© but let him have his Health, and all People elſe; and ſo to Drixk for 
© their own Health and Neceſſity only : For that way of Drinking 
* Healths, and to Exceſs, was not for the King's Health, nor their 
© own, nor any others, Which Exceſs often brought forth Quarrelling 
© and Deſtroying one another; for they deſtroyed the Creation, and 
© one another : And this was nat for the Kings Wealth, nor Health 
© nor Honour ; but might grieve him to have the Creatures deſtroyed, 
© and his Subjefts. And ſo, the Lord's Power gave us Dominion 
over that alſo, and all our other Sufferings. | | 

But Oh! the Number of Safferers in the Common Wealth's days, 
and in O. Protefor's days, and fince! Bur eſpecially they, that- were _ 
haled before their Corrs, for not Paying Tithes, and not Swearing in _ "gs od

we then ſuſtained upon theſe Accounts! For ſometimes they would TR 
drive Friends by Droves into the Priſon-houſes ( like Pexfo/ds) and 
there keep them on the Firſf-Days ; and then take their Horſes: from 
them, and keep them for pretended Breach of their Sabbath : Though 
they would Ride in their Coaches, and upon their 'Fat Horſes to 
the Steeple-houſes themſelves, and yet puniſh others. And many 
Fricads were turned out of their Copyholds and Cuftomary Tene- 
ments, becauſe they could not Swear ; And-as they. went to Meetings, 
they have been Stoned through the Streets; and cruelly abuſed: other- | 
wile, And many were Fined with great Fives, and lay long in S#fcring: for

And ſeveral Books T was moved to give forth againſt Swearing, and 
that our Tea and Nay might be taken inſtead of an Oath ; and if we 
broke that, let us ſuffer the ſame Puniſhment, that they did, that broke 
their Oaths. And in Famaica the Governor granted the thing, and the 
Aſſembly ; and it is alſo granted in ſome other Places : And ſeveral of 
the Parliament-Mex in England have acknowledged the Reaſonableneſs

by the Lord, and to ſay, and to do Truth, fince Man and Womaa fell, 
in the time of the Law, and not before the Fall : And this was the 
Oath, that Chrift came to fulfil and end ; and he faith, Swear not at 
all, AndI fay, Chrif fulfils and ends this Oath, which Men were to

himſelf, and fulfils that ; and he ſets up Tea, Yes, and Nay, Nay inftead 
thereof : Concerning which I and my Friends have written at large 
in our Books touching this Subjet. And the Magiſtrates, after ſome 
time, when they ſaw our Faithfulneſs in Tea and Nay, they that were 
Moderate ( both before and fince the Kzzz came in ) would put 
Friends into Offices without an Oath : But they that were Cruel and 
Envious, would fine Friends to get Money of them ; though Friends 
could not pay them any.

Ear Friends, Something was upon me to write unto you, that 
ſuch among Friends, who marry, and provide great Dinners, that 
inſtead: thereof, it will be of 'a” good Savoar on ſuch Occaſions, 
that they may be put in mind at ſuch times, to! give ſomething 
to the Poor that be Widows and Fatherleſs, and ſuch like, to'make 
them a Feaft, or to Refreſh them : And this, I look upon, would be 
a very good Savor, to feaſt the Poor that cannot feaſt you again ; 
and would be a good Practiſeand Example, and would: be a means:to 
keep the Mind to the Lord ; and in remembrance of the Poor ; for 
they that give to the Poor, lend to' the'Lord, and the Lord will re-pay they. 
And 1'do really believe, what ever they give, leſs or more, accordirs 
to their Ability, cheerfully, they will not have the-leſs at the Years 
End, for the Lord loves a cheerful Giver. I know this Praftice hath 
been uſed by ſome Twenty Years ago. And lo it is:not only to give 
the Poor a little Viftuals, which you cannot eat your ſelves, but give 
them a little Money, that the Lord hath bleſſed you with ; and give 
it to ſome of the Womens Meetings for to diſtribute to: the Poor : So 
you will have the Bleffings of the Lord, and the Bleſſings of the Poor': 
And fo, to be of a free noble $piriz, above all the churliſh Miſers and 
Nigards, and narrow Spirits | | 
Theſe things I do recommend to you ( though it may look a little 
ſtrange ) to weigh and conſider the thing, it will both be of a good 
Report, and a good Savour, and manifeſts a ſelf-denial and openneſs 
of Heart, and of the general Love of God, SENS.
